method_note: FAST MODE, one round. Reused facts copied from earlier packs with their sources (reused: true). New facts read today from official sources only.

facts.claim: Italy (US Embassy guidance): a civil ceremony is performed by the mayor or a deputy. Two witnesses (any nationality, over 18, valid photo ID) and, if needed, an interpreter must be present; a witness cannot serve as interpreter.
facts.publisher: US Embassy and Consulates in Italy
facts.use_note: Written for US citizens, but the ceremony itself is the same Italian civil ceremony for Australians (the comune runs it under the Italian Civil Code). Medium because the source is a US page; Italian official confirmation sought below. The comune (Ufficio di Stato Civile) confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italy: the US Embassy page does not bar relatives from being ceremony witnesses, while it does bar family members, future family members and in-laws from being Atto Notorio witnesses.
facts.publisher: US Embassy and Consulates in Italy
facts.use_note: Absence of a ban is not an explicit permission. Write 'relatives can usually witness the ceremony itself; confirm with the comune'. The comune confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italy, Australian route: Australians marrying in Italy need a Nulla Osta from the Australian Embassy in Rome. To get it, they first obtain an Atto Notorio, signed by the Australian citizen and four witnesses not related to the couple, either at the Italian consulate for their state of residence in Australia or at any tribunal in Italy. The Atto Notorio is valid 6 months.
facts.publisher: Consulate of Italy in Adelaide (Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
facts.use_note: These are paperwork witnesses, not ceremony witnesses. Keep the two apart in the article. The Italian consulate for the couple's state confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italy, US route only (for contrast): Italian consulates in New York and Los Angeles ask for four Atto Notorio witnesses over 18 and unrelated; San Francisco says two witnesses per spouse; the US Embassy page says two.
facts.publisher: Consolato Generale d'Italia a New York
facts.use_note: DO NOT USE for Australians. Recorded to show it was checked. Australians follow F-102.

facts.claim: Greece (Heraklion): each person marrying must be accompanied by an adult witness. The witness may be a relative, even a first-degree one, and must bring an identity card or, for foreigners, a passport.
facts.use_note: Two witnesses in total. Other municipalities may differ. The municipality's civil registry (Lixiarchio) confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Fiji: foreigners marrying in Fiji need passports, a Certificate of Single Status, Certificate of Search or Certificate of No Legal Impediment, divorce or death papers if relevant, and two witnesses with photo ID.
facts.use_note: No minimum age stated on this page. The Registrar General's Office (Fiji BDM) confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: a marriage must take place at a town hall (mairie) to be legally recognised, and at least one of the applicants must be a French citizen or a legal resident of France.
facts.use_note: Witness rules matter only if one partner qualifies. The mairie confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Indonesia (including Bali): for non-Muslim marriages, couples lodge a Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before the wedding and the marriage must be registered there to be legal. Both parties must hold the same religion recognised by the Indonesian Government.
facts.use_note: Context for witness facts. The Civil Registry Office (Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil) confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Greece (Heraklion, general civil marriage page): two witnesses over 18, one for each person marrying, must attend the ceremony and sign the marriage certificate; for foreign nationals a piece of identification is required.
facts.use_note: Read from the search result summary only, not the full page, so medium. Consistent with F-110 (same municipality). Witnesses sign the marriage certificate. The municipality's civil registry confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Greece, ceremonies at Greek consular offices (Greek Embassy in London page): two witnesses with a valid passport or ID card must be present, regardless of degree of relatedness. The Greek mission in the UAE instead asks for two Greek citizens as witnesses.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Embassy of Greece in London
facts.use_note: Applies to weddings at a Greek consulate, not at a Greek town hall. Read from search summary only, and two missions conflict (London vs UAE https://www.mfa.gr/missionsabroad/en/uae-en/other-services/civil-wedding.html). Do not use for a wedding in Greece. Recorded for completeness.

facts.claim: France: witnesses are compulsory for a marriage. The couple choose 2 witnesses minimum and 4 maximum; they are witnesses of the marriage, not of one partner.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative (French Prime Minister's office)
facts.use_note: Page meta description says 'minimum 1 and maximum 2 for each spouse', same total. Legal basis cited on the page: Code civil article 37. The mairie confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: witnesses must be at least 18 (or emancipated) on the day. No other condition: they can be family members or not, of any sex, and of foreign nationality. A witness who does not understand French may be assisted by an interpreter of their choice.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative (French Prime Minister's office)
facts.use_note: Good line for the article: Australian friends and family can be witnesses in France. The mairie confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: witnesses are declared during the pre-marriage formalities (surname, given names, date and place of birth, occupation, address, plus a copy of each witness's ID) and can be changed until the ceremony. They must bring their ID on the day and stay for the whole ceremony until they sign the register. They certify the couple's identity and the accuracy of their declarations. If a witness does not show, the registrar may find one (for example a town hall staff member) but is not obliged to.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative (French Prime Minister's office)
facts.use_note: The marriage certificate records each witness's name, occupation, address and majority. The mairie confirms the current process. Reminder: F-120 residency rule limits who can legally marry in France.

facts.claim: France (dossier de mariage page): each witness must present the original of their identity document on the day of the ceremony.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative (French Prime Minister's office)
facts.use_note: Confirms F-123. The mairie confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Indonesia: Government Regulation (PP) No. 9 of 1975, implementing Marriage Law No. 1 of 1974, article 10: following the procedure of each religion or belief, the marriage takes place before the Registrar (Pegawai Pencatat) and is attended by two witnesses ('dihadiri oleh dua orang saksi').
facts.publisher: Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan RI (Indonesian Audit Board) legal database
facts.use_note: Medium: the article text was confirmed via search excerpts (Wikisource and DPR copy https://berkas.dpr.go.id/jdih/document/pp/3520.pdf), not read in full on the BPK page this round. The regulation states the number only; no age, ID or relationship rule found in an official source. The Civil Registry Office in Bali confirms the current process.

needs.topic: Italy: Italian official source for ceremony witnesses
needs.detail: Ceremony witness rules (two, over 18, photo ID, witness cannot be interpreter) come only from the US Embassy page (F-100). The Italian Civil Code art. 107 basis and an Italian comune page stating relatives may be witnesses were seen only in secondary summaries (a Comune di Mirandola rule quoted by trend-online.com; Comune di Modena note not fetched, timeout). Confirm with the comune's Ufficio di Stato Civile or fetch Normattiva art. 107 in round 2.

needs.topic: Greece: can a witness act as interpreter?
needs.detail: No official Greek source found on this. Non-official guides say the opposite of the brief (one witness often doubles as interpreter); Rethymno municipality reportedly requires a certified translator, but its page timed out. Do not state 'a witness cannot be the interpreter' for Greece. Confirm with the municipality.

needs.topic: Bali: witness age, ID and relationship
needs.detail: PP 9/1975 sets two witnesses (F-141). Over-18, passport ID, 'not direct blood relatives' and 'registry staff can witness' appear only on wedding-industry sites (Easy Weddings, Wedshed, planners). Confirm with the Denpasar or Badung Civil Registry Office or the Australian Consulate-General Bali.
Fiji MFA states two witnesses with photo ID (F-130) but no age. Confirm with Fiji BDM (Registrar General's Office, Suva).

self_check.legal_authority_noted: Each legal fact names the confirming authority (comune, municipality, mairie, civil registry, consulate, Fiji BDM), never the Wedded Advisor as authority.
